newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Anti-APEC forum blasts fantasy of borderless trade.
newsitem.headline: Anti-APEC forum blasts fantasy of borderless trade.

text.p: An anti-APEC conference held parallel to an annual summit of Asia-Pacific leaders in Manila said on Monday the region's politicians should give up the "fantasy" of borderless trade.

The Manila People's Forum on APEC, which wound up a four-day meeting of activists and non-governmental organisations on Sunday, said in a statement it recognised the importance of trade and rules to govern trade.

But it opposed the kind of trade represented by the APEC process of global economic integration "in service to a corporate agenda at the expense of the human rights, dignity and well-being of the peoples of this region."

The forum called on political leaders to give up the "fantasy" of a borderless world "and wake up to the reality that our legacy, our dignity, our culture and poor natural world are being drained away instead into the offshore accounts of global robber barons".

Leaders from the 18 member economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum were meeting in Manila on Monday to chart a course for a free trade zone covering half of humanity around the Pacific Rim by the year 2020.
The Philippine government, host to this year's summit, had sought to give APEC a "social face", the forum's statement said.

However at the same time it barred East Timorese Nobel Peace laureate and anti-Indonesian activist Jose Ramos Horta from the country "and repressed any form of protest for the duration of the APEC meetings", it said.
The Philippines barred Ramos Horta to prevent possible embarassment to Indonesian President Suharto, who was attending the APEC summit.

The declaration also called on governments to make the eradication of women's poverty a priority, deliver real social and economic justice, fight child labour and child prostitution, ensure labour and migrant labour rights and protect the environment.
The anti-APEC forum pledged to make itself felt at the 1997 APEC gathering in Vancouver, Canada.
